LESSON: WHOLE NUMBERS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.2: Whole Numbers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Whole Numbers, part of Numbers in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we get the next number in a pattern? 2. Why do we count numbers?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Whole Numbers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination: learner improvises place value tins and pockets from locally available materials.

• Communication and collaboration: learner discusses in groups the place value of digits written on the number cards.

Values:
• Unity: learner in turn, plays a game of putting number cards in place value tins or pockets according to the place

value of digits.

7

• Responsibility: learner observes safety precautions as they use locally available materials to improvise place value tins

and pockets.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Effective communication: learner reads and writes numbers 1 to 100 in symbols in different situations.

• Creative thinking: learner improvises place value tins and pockets from locally available materials.

Link to other learning areas:

• The learner relates the skills used in reading and writing numbers in symbols to reading and writing skills in English

Language Activities.

• The learner relates the skills used in making number patterns to the concept of patterns in Creative Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Bottle tops, marbles, sticks, stones, grains, a braille/ number line drawn on the ground/floor, number cards, braille cards,

digital devices, braille equipment’s and materials, print and braille charts.
